item.title: Snoop Dogg Helps Phonixthecool Build A Catalog He Owns
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Snoop Dogg's mentorship helped Phonixthecool build a catalog he owned while the Durban rapper worked toward Death Row releases.
item.content:encoded:
Snoop Dogg taught Phonixthecool how to earn from music he owned while Death Row Records developed the Durban rapper, the artist said.

In a new Sowetan interview, Phonixthecool described an arrangement that let him release songs on his own while work continued on his Death Row music. He said the goal was to keep an audience and build a catalog that could earn more once the label’s releases drew new listeners.

“Snoop has mentored me on monetising music and using his name while still releasing independently. That way, I own the music,” he said.

The rapper, born Lunga Khumalo, also described the work behind a signing: trying out producers and recording to find the right fit for his voice. He said people often expected a record deal to make an artist a star overnight.

His connection with Snoop reached listeners before the Death Row deal. Phonixthecool appeared with Battle Locco and Kokane on “No Smut On My Name” for 2021’s “Snoop Dogg Presents Algorithm (Global Edition),” released through Def Jam.

Snoop announced the signing in September 2023 while teasing Death Row Africa. By then, the label had become part of his own business, after years in which other companies controlled the name that helped launch his career.

He bought the Death Row brand from MNRK Music Group in February 2022. Funds managed by Blackstone controlled MNRK, and the companies did not disclose the price.

For Snoop, that move began with a desire to regain control of his own recordings. He told TIDAL in 2022 that Jimmy Iovine helped connect him with Blackstone’s David Kestnbaum because Iovine knew he wanted his masters.

“I don’t want to be on nobody’s label. But I’d be on Death Row if I own it. That’s a boss move,” Snoop said then.

He also described a hands-off approach to an artist’s sound. Rather than tell new signees how to rap, he wanted to give artists with a clear musical identity a bigger platform. He said his own experience as a rapper shaped how he handled label business.

Phonixthecool said their contact had mostly been through texts and FaceTime. He planned to visit Los Angeles in January 2027 for his first trip to the United States.

item.title: Nelly & Ashanti Turn Cameras On Her Masters Push & His Touring Grind
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Nelly and Ashanti's new season follows her push to own fresh recordings, his touring toll and their life between two cities.
item.content:encoded:
Nelly and Ashanti’s TV return will follow her push to control her music as he weighs the physical toll of nonstop touring.

Peacock confirmed Thursday that “Nelly and Ashanti: We Belong Together” returns November 19. All eight episodes of the second season will arrive that day, BroadwayWorld reported.

The new season follows Ashanti as she re-records her debut album, works on new music and moves between life in St. Louis and New York City. The season synopsis places that work alongside motherhood, live performances and time with the friends who help keep her grounded.

Nelly’s storyline will explore the physical strain of years on the road.

Ashanti’s ownership project has roots well before the couple’s reality series. She discussed plans to remake her first album during a 2021 appearance on “The Tamron Hall Show”, when she stressed the need to understand record contracts and credited her legal team.

Her self-titled debut, Ashanti, arrived in 2002 and included “Foolish,” “Happy” and “Baby.” The album earned triple-platinum certification.

Ashanti’s stated aim is to own new versions of those songs. Those new performances create separate master recordings from the versions released on her 2002 debut.

“I think it’s really important to stress the importance of ownership. Owning your records, owning your masters,” Ashanti told Rolling Stone AU/NZ in an earlier interview.

She urged artists to understand the business when writing and producing, and said she was re-recording her work. Her remarks put the project in the broader context of artists seeking more control over their creations.

She also singled out “Foolish” as a song that still draws a strong response at shows. Hearing thousands of fans sing words she wrote more than two decades ago remains a highlight of performing, she said.

That same interview offered a glimpse of their offstage chemistry: Ashanti picked Nelly as her favorite collaborator. He joined the video call, joked, “Just making sure,” and kissed her cheek.

The couple’s show was renewed in March 2026 after its June 2025 debut. They began dating in 2003, reunited in 2023 and married that year. The new eight-episode season arrives in full on November 19.

item.title: Lil Wayne Backs Shedeur Sanders Staying In Cleveland After Young Money Deal
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Lil Wayne backed Shedeur Sanders getting his chance in Cleveland after the Browns quarterback hired a Young Money APAA agent.
item.content:encoded:
Lil Wayne backed Shedeur Sanders’ future with the Cleveland Browns after the quarterback hired an agent from the rapper’s Young Money APAA Sports firm.

Asked on “Gridiron” whether he wanted Sanders to leave Cleveland, Wayne made clear he wanted to see the quarterback get his chance where he is. Pro Football Network reported the exchange from his new appearance with Skip Bayless.

“Also, I need him to get his opportunity, and I think where he is, he’s going to get that opportunity,” Wayne said.

The comments carried a business connection beyond Wayne’s interest in football. Sanders hired Young Money APAA CEO Adie von Gontard as his first NFL agent, as AllHipHop reported earlier this week. He went through the draft and the start of his pro career without one.

Wayne did not discuss that hire in his answer. He expressed confidence in Sanders’ future in Cleveland without announcing a move or speaking for the quarterback about his plans.

Cleveland’s current depth chart lists Deshaun Watson first and Sanders second. Head coach Todd Monken chose Watson to open the season after weighing their work through the offseason, training camp, a joint practice and preseason games.

Monken explained in August that the Browns’ opening road games helped shape his choice. He believed Watson gave the team the best chance to run the offense in those settings, including handling the noise and signals away from home.

Since then, Sanders has had little room to show what he can do. Through Cleveland’s first five games, team stats listed one pass, completed for no gain against Carolina. The Browns entered the weekend with a 3-2 record.

Sanders had a larger role as a rookie in 2025. He completed 120 of 212 passes for 1,400 yards, with seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions, before returning to a backup role this season.

Young Money’s ties to Sanders’ former college team already ran through Travis Hunter. The agency represents the Jacksonville Jaguars player, who played alongside Sanders at Colorado. Wayne co-founded the firm with the von Gontard family, and Adie is a certified NFL Players Association agent.

The league’s trade deadline is November 10 at 4 p.m. Eastern.

item.title: RZA Relives Panic Over Wu-Tang’s Martin Shkreli Deal
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: RZA accepted Martin Shkreli's place in Wu-Tang history as a new film traced the rare album's troubled path from art to asset.
item.content:encoded:
RZA recalled trying to escape the Martin Shkreli album deal after the buyer’s drug-price scandal, but said a signed contract blocked that exit.

He recounted the panic in a new interview with PEOPLE. Years after the 2015 sale, he accepted Shkreli’s place in Wu-Tang’s story.

“Yes, to be honest. Yes. You got to accept that,” RZA said.

His comments came as “The Disciple: A Wu-Tang Fable” reached streaming. The film follows Cilvaringz, born Tarik Azzougarh, a Dutch-Moroccan rapper who pursued a place within Wu-Tang. His bond with RZA led to the rare album Once Upon a Time in Shaolin.

The 31-track project challenged the idea that recorded music should be cheap and easy to copy. Its creators offered one physical album in a silver box. Shkreli bought it for a reported $2 million in 2015.

RZA, an executive producer and subject of the film, also addressed the work’s future in Netflix’s updated profile. He said he no longer needed to control where it went.

“This has become an entity of its own, and we should allow it to live,” he said.

The album’s path later ran through a federal fraud case. A Brooklyn jury convicted Shkreli in August 2017 of two counts of securities fraud and one count of conspiracy. He cheated investors and rigged a drug company’s stock. A judge sentenced him to seven years in prison.

Shkreli had to give up the record to help pay a roughly $7.4 million judgment. Prosecutors announced its sale on July 27, 2021, saying the money cleared that debt. The case concerned fraud, separate from the drug-pricing scandal RZA recalled.

The concept also caused friction within Wu-Tang. As AllHipHop previously reported, Method Man said in 2024 that members recorded verses without knowing how Cilvaringz would package them. He described the album as a difficult subject within the group.

RZA also said the project had brought him enemies, praise and questions. A small audience could still carry its ideas forward, in his view.

Director Joanna Natasegara said the album challenged how the music business valued art, especially work by artists of color. Her film follows Cilvaringz’s drive to join the group and turn that idea into one rare record. It began streaming October 16.

item.title: Juvenile Scraps Minneapolis Show After Two Earlier Delays
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Juvenile canceled his Minneapolis concert after two earlier delays, with refunds planned and no new date for ticket holders.
item.content:encoded:
Juvenile canceled his October 21 Minneapolis show after two earlier delays, leaving First Avenue ticket holders with a refund plan and no replacement date, according to the venue and a new local report.

For online and phone purchases through AXS, First Avenue gave a window of up to 30 business days for automatic refunds. The money will return to the card charged for the tickets. Refunds for tickets purchased elsewhere are handled by the seller. AXS support and its app are the venue’s listed contacts for ticket help.

The page still contains old instructions to keep tickets for a rescheduled show. Its cancellation notice at the top gives the current refund directions.

Bring Me The News reported October 17 that the concert had first been set for July 14, then August 9, before moving to October. First Avenue’s artist page lists both earlier 2026 dates as postponed. Those shifts stretched the local booking across more than three months.

The local outlet said Juvenile had offered no explanation, and his representatives did not immediately respond to its request for comment. Its report landed four days before the planned show.

The canceled date was billed as the “Boiling Point Album Release Tour” with The 400 Degreez Band & Friends, presented by Carbon Sound. Juvenile released the album earlier this year. The show was a return to a room where he and the band played with Mannie Fresh on October 2, 2024, during his “Back That Azz Up 25th Anniversary Tour.”

That live-band approach also shaped his 2023 “Tiny Desk Concert” in NPR’s Washington, D.C., offices. Fans had urged him to do that performance after he initially dismissed the idea. The lineup included Mannie Fresh, Trombone Shorty and Jon Batiste, with Louisiana Philharmonic strings for the finale. They performed songs including “Ha,” “Slow Motion” and “Back That Azz Up,” with the audience calling for an encore.

Other stops remain on Juvenile’s official tour page, which now starts with October 22 at Lincoln, Nebraska’s Bourbon Theatre. St. Louis on October 23 and Memphis on October 24 follow. Minneapolis is absent from that itinerary. First Avenue’s notice states, “There is no rescheduled date at this time.”

item.title: Tank Breaks Charlie Wilson’s Adult R&B Record With “Yes”
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Tank earned his 12th Adult R&B Airplay No. 1 with "Yes," passing Charlie Wilson after a comeback shaped by hearing loss.
item.content:encoded:
Tank passed Charlie Wilson for the most No. 1 hits by a male artist on Billboard’s Adult R&B Airplay chart as “Yes” became his 12th chart-topper.

The single took the lead on the chart dated October 17, ending the two singers’ tie at 11. Billboard confirmed the new record in its latest chart rundown. Alicia Keys still holds the overall lead with 14 No. 1s.

Wilson had reached 11 with “Keep Me In Love” in October 2025. Tank caught up this year when “Control” topped the chart, giving him a share of the male record before “Yes” moved him ahead.

The win added a new high to the rollout of “EXPERIENCE”, which arrived through R&B Money/BMG. “Yes” draws on Floetry’s “Say Yes,” bringing a song from an earlier R&B era into his new album.

The track also led Mediabase’s U.S. R&B chart for the week of October 10, rising from No. 3. It had spent 13 weeks on that chart, giving the singer another radio win as the new album reached listeners.

Getting back to this point meant working through a health scare that had shaken his career. Tank disclosed his hearing loss in 2021, telling fans he was losing hearing in his right ear and struggling with sound in his left. He also described dizziness and trouble walking a straight line while he sought treatment.

He later billed his 2022 album “R&B Money” as his last. In a recent Men’s Health interview, Tank recalled how hearing loss and vertigo had disrupted his life. Medication affected his sleep and eating, and he struggled to work out.

“I didn’t recognize myself. I couldn’t hear myself,” Tank said. “First time I was ever out of shape in life.”

He discussed rebuilding his fitness and confidence to return to the stage.

Tank had already built years of radio success before his health scare. His hit “When We” had spent a year on the charts by 2018, when he spoke with the Recording Academy backstage at Essence Festival about his outlook.

“As long as you’re putting in the work, at some point…there will be a harvest,” Tank told the Recording Academy.

item.title: Marsha Blackburn Offers No Apology Over Kendrick Lamar AI Clip
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Marsha Blackburn's Kendrick Lamar AI defense came months after she demanded the removal of an AI attack ad targeting her.
item.content:encoded:
Marsha Blackburn said she never meant to offend Black Americans with her campaign’s AI remake of Kendrick Lamar’s Super Bowl performance, offering a new defense without an apology.

The Tennessee Republican faced a direct question about that criticism when FOX13 reporter Rob Sneed caught up with her after a public safety roundtable in Shelby County on Friday. He also asked whether she understood the song’s lyrics and the reaction to the clip.

“We, there would never be any action that was intended to offend,” Blackburn said.

She again credited a county commissioner with making the video and said her campaign shared it because she thought it was fun. Her campaign’s stated priorities included affordability and public safety, alongside education, health care and infrastructure.

The answer added to a dispute that began when Blackburn posted the clip October 13 to promote early voting in her run for governor. The AI scene put her in Kendrick Lamar’s place and turned fellow Tennessee Republicans into dancers as “Not Like Us” played.

Her Democratic opponent, Jerri Green, had already criticized the use of AI in the campaign. Blackburn’s earlier description of the post as a “funsie” also preceded the new question about Black Americans who found it offensive.

The controversy touches a cause Blackburn has championed in Washington: protecting people from digital copies made without their consent. In June, she and Chris Coons announced that their NO FAKES proposal had cleared the Senate Judiciary Committee. Her office described safeguards for voices and visual likenesses, with exceptions for protected speech.

Blackburn had also sought protection from AI campaign content herself. In July, she demanded that the American Exceptionalism Institute PAC remove an AI attack ad within 48 hours and disclose its use of the technology, WPLN reported.

That ad accused her of taking drug-industry money in exchange for legislation. Her letter denied that she ever accepted a bribe to pass a bill. The two disputes involved different uses of AI: one made an allegation against Blackburn, while her post recast a music performance as a voting pitch. Her spokesperson told WPLN that two TV stations had pulled the attack ad.

item.title: 50 Cent Slams The Door On Courtney Kemp As “Power” Creator Hits Back
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: 50 Cent ruled out another Courtney Kemp project as the "Power" creator disputed his claims about their hit TV partnership.
item.content:encoded:
50 Cent ruled out working with Courtney Kemp again, and the “Power” creator pushed back on his claims about their work.

“I don’t look forward to working with her ever again,” he told Variety in a new interview.

The rapper felt Kemp had lost sight of his role in selling the show. He pointed to the music he made for pitches and his work to get the series off the ground.

Kemp challenged his budget claims and his grasp of how the show was run. She also denied that she had played down his part in its success.

“I have never once understated his importance in the genesis of ‘Power,'” she said.

Their roles were clear when Starz first picked up the show in 2013. Kemp created the crime drama and took on the job of showrunner, while 50 joined as an executive producer. The network’s first order was for eight episodes.

That grew into a much bigger deal. The first “Power” ran for six seasons and ended in 2020. Its spinoffs kept key characters on screen as the show branched out into a string of new stories.

Music was part of the show’s sound from the start. 50’s “Big Rich Town” video, with Joe, came out in April 2014 before the show’s debut. Starz also offered the video as a first-season bonus.

In 2021, Kemp signed a Netflix deal and passed the day-to-day work on “Power Book II: Ghost” to Brett Mahoney before its third season. She kept an executive producer role in the “Power” shows.

Her move to a new home for her own shows came years before this latest clash over credit. Both Kemp and 50 still had executive producer credits for that third season of “Ghost.”

Kemp went on to create “Nemesis” with Tani Marole. The eight-part Netflix crime drama came out in May and followed a Los Angeles cop and a master thief. It was the first show from her deal with the streamer. Netflix ordered a second season in June.

The work she and 50 built together also found a new home. A Netflix rights deal included U.S. rights to the original “Power” and international rights to its first four series, with the rollout set for November.

Kemp said she had moved on in her career and hoped 50’s “Street Fighter” success would help him do the same.

item.title: Eminem Defends Kid Rock Collab With Message About Their Friendship
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Eminem explained why he teamed with Kid Rock as their new song put a long friendship back under the glare of political debate.
item.content:encoded:
Eminem defended his new song with Kid Rock on October 17. He said an old friendship brought them back together despite the clash over their politics.

The rapper shared his stance on X as “Heal My Faith” arrived on Rock’s new Christian album, “Halfway 2 Jesus.”

He wrote, “Not about choosing sides, just choosing to make music with my old friend. Praying for all of us.”

His post tagged Kid Rock and used the song’s hashtag. It put the focus on their bond after weeks of debate over the pairing.

Rock backs Donald Trump. Eminem has long criticized him. He appeared at a Detroit rally for Kamala Harris in October 2024. He urged the crowd to vote before he brought former President Barack Obama to the stage.

At that event, he also spoke about the right to express one’s views without fear of payback. Obama then walked out to “Lose Yourself” and rapped part of the hit.

Kid Rock told Fox News this month that he and Eminem had refused to let politics break their friendship.

The new statement follows a change in the album’s guest list. AllHipHop reported that Rock posted a new tracklist on October 14. It put Lil Wayne on “7 Sins,” where fans had first expected to hear Eminem.

That change did not mean Eminem had left the project. Rock kept him on the fifth track, “Heal My Faith,” while Wayne took the third slot. Rock used a video to spell out the switch for fans who had objected to the joint record.

Their ties stretch back well before this dispute. Eminem appeared on “F#ck Off” from Rock’s 1998 album “Devil Without A Cause.” Rock later made a cameo in Eminem’s “Berzerk” video.

Consequence reports that the new song reaches back to one of Rock’s early shows of support. In his verse, Eminem recalls Rock attending the release party for “The Slim Shady EP” while he was still unknown. He casts their bond as one that can survive how each man votes. Rock ends the track with a spoken message about their friendship and the freedom to hold different views.

item.title: MGK’s Car At Dakota Johnson’s House Adds To Dating Buzz
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: MGK and Dakota Johnson left an LA studio together as photos of his car at her home added to weeks of dating speculation.
item.content:encoded:
Machine Gun Kelly and Dakota Johnson left a Los Angeles studio together on October 15, adding a late-night stop to the outings that have fueled dating rumors.

Page Six, in a report carried by AOL, said Johnson waited outside while the rapper finished a recording session. She wore a leopard-print coat and held what appeared to be a laptop.

When MGK came out, he moved a bag from the front seat into his trunk. Johnson then got into his Maserati, and the pair left together.

The next morning, his car remained parked at Johnson’s home, the account said. The outlet described the outing as an apparent overnight stay based on photos of the vehicle outside her house.

The pair had also stepped out at Hollywood’s Say Yes lounge earlier in the week, extending a run of sightings that began drawing attention in September.

Us Weekly traced their New York outing to September 11, when they visited Taylor Swift’s Tribeca apartment before going to dinner at Estela. An unnamed source described the visit as a date and said Swift had offered the space because the two wanted privacy.

They had also attended Swift and Travis Kelce’s wedding in July, which sources pointed to as the start of their connection.

Later in September, another source described them as “seriously dating” and said they had kept in touch daily. Johnson also attended the Vogue World: Milano show, where MGK walked the runway on September 22.

The sightings followed high-profile breakups for both stars. MGK and Megan Fox split in late 2024, while Johnson’s eight-year relationship with Coldplay frontman Chris Martin ended in 2025. She later dated singer Role Model before their split this summer.

Johnson addressed the rush to label her outings during a September appearance on Vogue’s “The Run-Through” podcast. She said even dinner with her manager or lawyer could trigger headlines about a mystery man. Asked whether she wanted to correct such stories, she said she preferred to put her energy elsewhere.

“People are gonna believe what they wanna believe, and I don’t have the energy to fight for that,” Johnson said.
